description: Future North Atlantic tropical cyclone intensities in modified historical environments is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Nicholas Lalo et al. Tropical cyclones (TCs) have ranked as the deadliest and most financially crippling natural disasters in the United States. It is imperative to assess potential shifts in TC intensity within the paradigm of an evolving climate. Coverage: national (US); published in 2025. Formats: NetCDF. The data are held in Pacific Northwest National Lab (United States) and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence of the data is not stated in the sources read (the paper itself is open access). Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
